newsitem.title: USA: Coke results may bode well for PepsiCo.
newsitem.headline: Coke results may bode well for PepsiCo.

text.p: Coca-Cola Co's first-quarter results showed unusually strong unit case sales growth in the U.S. soft-drink market, which could actually bode well for arch-rival PepsiCo Inc, analysts said on Monday.

The beverage group reported domestic unit case sales growth at nine percent for the quarter, its best quarterly showing in the United States in at least five years, according to analysts. As a result, some on Wall Street estimated Coca-Cola's share of the U.S. market at 43 percent, up from 42 percent just three months ago.
"With a nine percent gain, the (market) share's moving up. They're getting off to an awfully nice start this year," said Manny Goldman at PaineWebber.

Although Coke's expansion could mean a U.S. market-share loss for PepsiCo, analysts say new packaging and aggressive marketing campaigns by both companies have helped create a robust market for carbonated beverages overall.
"(Coke's) doing nine percent and Pepsi will do about six. Versus Pepsi for the quarter, there was a share gain. Whether that will be the case for the full year, we'll have to see," Goldman added.
Analysts expect PepsiCo's first-quarter earnings to be flat at $0.24 per share, when it releases first-quarter financial results on April 29, according to First Call.
In U.S. beverages, PepsiCo's volume growth would be driven by strong sales at supermarkets, as well as a competitive push against Coke for sales at convenience locations.

Aside from an expected decline in soft-drink sales overseas, analysts say investors also could see mid-to-high single-digit growth at Frito-Lay in the Unted States, with a double-digit earnings gain overseas; a double-digit earnings gain at KFC and a modest volume rise for Taco Bell.

Analysts also expect a volume decline in the high single-digit range at Pizza Hut. But the outlook for Pepsi calls for gradual improvement as the year moves forward, especially in trouble spots such as overseas beverage sales.
According to First Call, analysts expect PepsiCo to earn 1.46 per share this year, excluding restructuring charges and other non-recurring against last year's $1.17 per share.

"More important to me than the actual bottom line earnings is going to be unit volume sales in soft-drinks and in snacks and any sign of progress in restaurants," said David Goldman at Robinson-Humphrey in Atlanta.
"I'd be surprised if, when 1997 is over, Pepsi is not reporting the same soft-drink volume gains globally that Coke is reporting, maybe even a bit better.

"The biggest factor I'm looking at Pepsi for in the first quarter and all through 1997 is going to be the rate of improvement they can show from a very disappointing year in two specific areas: restaurants with a focus on Pizza Hut and international soft-drinks."

Meanwhile, despite some worries about the strength of the dollar and its possible effect on future Coke earnings, analysts say marketing and packaging initiatives by the Atlanta-based company have begun expanding its role worldwide.
"The company's gaining market share in almost every single soft-drink market in the world," said Oppenheimer's Roy Burry.
